report.headline: Playmaking G Leaguer projected for a smaller offensive role in the NBA, with the shooting-efficiency forecast carrying no real signal

projection.text: The model projects a usage rate of 15.7% in the NBA, down from 19.3% in the G League and below the league-average 20.1% (sd 5.2%), with an 80% interval of 10.5%–20.9% and a 95% interval of 7.7%–23.7%.

risks.text: A high turnover rate of 23.4% in the source season is a red flag for ball-handling reliability at a higher level of competition.
Projected usage of 15.7% sits nearly a full standard deviation below the NBA average of 20.1% (sd 5.2%), implying a materially reduced offensive role.

The shooting-efficiency projection is unreliable: the model does not beat a trivial league-average baseline on true shooting percentage, so downside or upside on that metric cannot be responsibly forecast.
The estimate rests on only 45 historical G League to NBA transitions, a thin cohort for pinning down individual outcomes.

strengths.text: Strong playmaking indicators in the source season: a 25.8% assist rate and 6.21 assists per 75 possessions.
Efficient scoring relative to the G League, posting a 57.5% true shooting percentage, 0.39 standard deviations above the league average.
A perimeter-oriented shot profile, with 34.3% of attempts coming from three.

uncertainty.text: The true shooting projection of 53.0% (80% interval 47.2%–58.7%, 95% interval 44.2%–61.8%) comes from a model whose out-of-fold error (4.7%) is identical to simply guessing the league mean (4.7%), so this number should not be treated as informative about likely shooting efficiency.
